obligations.mechanism: CMS_add0_recipient_password writes RAND_bytes_ex(ivlen) into unsigned char iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH] and then hands the same buffer to EVP_EncryptInit_ex
obligations.pre_fix: ivlen = EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_iv_length(ctx); if (ivlen < 0) break; if (ivlen > 0) RAND_bytes_ex(libctx, iv.as_mut_ptr(), ivlen as usize, 0); with iv declared [0u8; EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH] (16). Only the negative arm was rejected; a length above 16 reached RAND_bytes_ex and EVP_EncryptInit_ex unchecked.
obligations.fix: After the authority's existing ivlen < 0 arm, refuse ivlen as usize > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:305) and break to the function's err tail (ctx and encalg released, NULL returned). The refusal raises CMS_PWRI_IV_REFUSED (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:56): ERR_LIB_CMS, ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT, authority coordinates crypto/cms/cms_pwri.c:107, the RAND_bytes_ex call the conversion declines. This is the same shape as the landed S27 pk7_doit refusal.

reachability.in_tree: NOT reachable. grep over src/ finds no Rust caller of CMS_add0_recipient_password (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:107 defines it; cms_smime.rs uses CMS_RecipientInfo_set0_password instead). The only in-tree route to the setup block is the exported C ABI.
reachability.from_parsed_der_only: NOT reachable. CMS_EncryptedContentInfo.cipher is at offset 24 of the #[repr(C)] struct (src/cms/cms_asn1.rs:206-218), but CMS_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_INFO_TT has only three template columns, at offsets 0, 8 and 16 (src/cms/cms_asn1.rs:1291-1313: contentType, contentEncryptionAlgorithm, encryptedContent). A parsed object therefore leaves ec.cipher/ec.key NULL and the NULL-kekciph arm raises CMS_R_NO_CIPHER (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:141-151) before the IV block.
reachability.reachable_at_the_c_abi: YES. The exported function takes kekciph: *const c_void (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:108), and ec.cipher is set by the exported CMS_EnvelopedData_create(cipher) (src/cms/cms_env.rs:489-545 via ossl_cms_EncryptedContent_init at src/cms/cms_enc.rs:534). A METH cipher built by EVP_CIPHER_meth_new carries any block_size/key_len and EVP_CIPHER_meth_set_iv_length stores any int without a bound (src/evp/cipher.rs:1457-1473,1538-1550); a METH cipher is routed to the legacy init path by origin == EVP_ORIG_METH (src/evp/cipher_ctx.rs:1942-1957), so its reported iv_len is what EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_iv_length returns (src/evp/cipher_ctx.rs:825-889). A provider cipher's ivlen is an unbounded size_t cached into an int (src/evp/cipher_ctx.rs:833-886; src/evp/cipher.rs:1186-1192). Either form reaches the write if an application maps untrusted input to the cipher, or loads a provider reporting ivlen > 16.
reachability.demonstrated: cms_pwri_oversized_iv_is_refused drives a METH AES-128-CBC method with iv_len 32 through CMS_add0_recipient_password on a CMS_EnvelopedData_create object. Pre-fix that call reached RAND_bytes_ex(libctx, iv.as_mut_ptr(), 32, 0) and EVP_EncryptInit_ex(..., iv) with iv: [u8; 16].
reachability.conclusion: Not in-tree; reachable only through the C ABI (application-selected METH/provider cipher or a custom provider). No claim of attacker reachability without application cooperation. The precondition is now structural regardless of which cipher definitions exist.

obligations.divergence: A length the authority would write past a stack buffer is refused before the write, with NULL plus ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT (AGENTS.md section 17, UB in the C authority: do not reproduce). Every length that fits keeps the authority's control flow.

obligations.mechanism: kek_wrap_key reads in[0], in[1], in[2] as the RFC 3211 header without establishing that three bytes are readable
obligations.pre_fix: The only length guards were blocklen == 0, olen < 2 * blocklen and inlen > 0xFF. The round-up olen = (inlen + 4).div_ceil(blocklen) * blocklen does not imply inlen >= 3: with blocklen == 4 and inlen == 2, olen == 8 == 2 * blocklen, so the header body ran and read two bytes past the input; with blocklen == 1 and inlen == 0 it read one byte past an empty input.
obligations.fix: Explicit inlen < 3 refusal before the round-up and before any pointer use (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:662), returning the authority's silent 0. The header SAFETY comment now cites the checked condition (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:690-692). The round-up now uses checked_add/checked_mul and returns 0 on overflow (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:672-681), and a non-positive block size is refused before the cast to usize (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:651-657).

reachability.in_tree: No caller of kek_wrap_key outside this file (grep src/). Its one caller is the encryption arm of ossl_cms_RecipientInfo_pwri_crypt (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:936-960), which passes ec.key/ec.keylen. On the encrypt path ec.keylen is set by ossl_cms_EncryptedContent_init_bio from EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_key_length of the content cipher and refused when that is <= 0 (src/cms/cms_enc.rs:355-365,392-398), and the KEK block length comes from the DER-selected keyEncryptionAlgorithm. With the in-tree ciphers inspected (AES wrap block 8; AES/DES/3DES/Camellia/ARIA/SM4 block 8 or 16) the olen < 2 * blocklen check rejects inlen < 3 before the header, so the in-tree path is not reachable. No exhaustive cipher enumeration was performed.
reachability.reachable_at_the_c_abi: YES, via a METH/provider KEK cipher whose block size is 1..4 (EVP_CIPHER_meth_new accepts any block_size, src/evp/cipher.rs:1457-1473) combined with a short content key. A content cipher can report key_len 1 or 2, and ossl_cms_EncryptedContent_init_bio only refuses key lengths <= 0 (src/cms/cms_enc.rs:356-365), so an application that supplies both ciphers can reach the header with inlen == 2 and blocklen == 4.
reachability.internal_contract: Independently of external reachability, the function's own # Safety contract only required `in` readable for `inlen` (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:636-638). A caller satisfying that contract with inlen < 3 and a 4-byte-block context could drive an out-of-bounds read, which is a soundness defect at the internal boundary. The guard removes it.
reachability.demonstrated: cms_pwri_short_wrap_input_is_refused_before_any_read calls kek_wrap_key with a live 4-byte-block METH context, inlen == 2 and a NULL input pointer. The guard returns 0 before any `*input`; a regression would fault in the test itself. The output buffer is asserted untouched and outlen stays 0.

obligations.divergence: Inputs the authority reads past (UB in the C authority) return 0 instead, which is the same result the authority's own length checks return for the neighbouring cases. Inputs of three or more bytes are unchanged.

obligations.mechanism: review of the remaining short-input arithmetic in the file (scope check, no change)
obligations.evidence: kek_unwrap_key requires blocklen >= 4 and inlen >= 2 * blocklen >= 8 before reading raw[1..7], rejects a non-multiple and > INT_MAX, and checks inlen < 4 + raw[0] before the bounded copy (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:529-630). In the unwrap arm of pwri_crypt, a negative encrypted_key->length becomes a usize allocation request through the seam, which returns None and breaks (src/cms/cms_pwri.rs:941-960); the authority's OPENSSL_malloc fails the same way, so no UB and no semantic change was introduced. This path was not modified.

production_unsafe_tokens.note: One new unsafe operation: raise_site(&CMS_PWRI_IV_REFUSED), carrying a SAFETY comment ('the site is a compile-time constant'). The bound checks and the checked arithmetic are safe Rust.

structural_guards.note: git diff -U0 shows no added or removed line containing CRYPTO_, SeamFile, no_mangle or repr(C). The three SeamFile::new(c"cms_pwri.c") sites (lines 557, 942, 979) keep their authority file and line (219, 392, 403). No allocation size changed.

not_established: No in-tree cipher was exhaustively enumerated for iv_len > 16 or for block sizes below 5; the in-tree non-reachability statements are limited to the route found by source inspection and the cipher definitions inspected, and the guards are enforced independently of that enumeration.

Attacker reachability without application cooperation is excluded for the IV path by the C-ABI-only call graph and the DER template shape; a downstream application that maps untrusted input to a fetched or METH cipher is out of this file's scope and was not audited.

The short-wrap C-ABI route (custom KEK cipher with block size 1..4 plus a 1- or 2-byte content key) is established from the exported setter/init behaviour and a direct internal test, not by driving a full CMS_encrypt with two custom ciphers.
Full library suite, adversarial probes, Miri/ASan and differential courts were not run (FAST gate only).
The pre-existing raise_cms helper records file cms_lib.c for all cms_pwri raise sites; the new refusal uses its own ErrSite for that reason, but the existing sites were not changed in this batch.
